//models: Implementer model and effort per ticket Size. Implementers were 69% of the first run's token bill, so this is the main dial — but the dial is EFFORT, not a weaker model. Lower effort on the strongest model beats a cheaper model at high effort, and it keeps one cache namespace. Downgrading the implementer is a false economy on a codebase with real conventions: one extra fix round costs another implementer session plus a review, which is more than the tokens a smaller model saved, and it buys worse code. Set a Size to sonnet only for genuinely mechanical work (the same small edit across files), and only if you have watched it hold up in your codebase.
//reviewRule: THE REVIEWER IS NEVER WEAKER THAN THE IMPLEMENTER. A previous-generation model of the same family is not independence, it is a downgrade — Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 cost the same $5/$25 per Mtok, so reviewing Opus 5's work with 4.8 buys nothing and loses capability. Independence comes from a DIFFERENT family (Codex gpt-6-astra by default); when that is unavailable, review with the implementer's tier or one above it.
